subject: Order Form + SLA redlines (uptime, credits, response times)
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@nimbus.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@nimbus.io
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Nimbus redlines to Order Form and SLA - initial

Hi Irene / Rishi,

Attached is Nimbus Cloud's redline of the Order Form and the SLA section in the MSA. High-level asks from our legal and infra teams:

- Uptime target: ask to change the financial availability from 99.9% to 99.95% (monthly).
- Service credits: propose a linear credit scale that starts at 0.5% credit for <99.95 and scales to 15% for <99.0.
- Response times: clarify P1/P2 windows and require a formal 24/7 escalation path with named contacts.
- Maintenance: require 72-hour advance notice for scheduled maintenance that may cause degraded performance (not just outages).

We flagged a few ambiguous clauses in the redline (Nimbus_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx). Can we get Redwood's commercial/legal view on the above and whether Redwood can commit to those targets or propose alternates?

We can do a short call if helpful — happy to coordinate availability.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Chen
Director, Procurement
Nimbus Cloud

Attachments: Nimbus_OrderForm_v3_redline.docx

Subject: Re: Nimbus redlines to Order Form and SLA - initial

Laura — thanks for sending this over and the clear summary. I looped in Rishi (legal lead), Dev (platform ops) and Marissa (CS) so we can get a coordinated response.

Quick reaction and next steps:
- We reviewed the uptime ask. 99.95% is higher than our standard for equivalent committed capacity; we'll outline the technical guarantees and an alternative Escrow/penalty approach in the matrix. See attached Redwood_SLA_matrix.xlsx for a draft counter proposal on target bands and credit caps.
- Service credits: we generally cap credits to a percentage of the monthly invoice; we'll propose a tiered schedule but ask Nimbus to accept a maximum annual cap to mitigate unlimited liability.
- Response times / escalation: agree that a named escalation path is necessary; Dev will propose operating hours for different support tiers and how P1 paging behaves across regions.
- Maintenance notifications: 72 hours for changes that cause degraded performance is reasonable for planned maintenance that affects availability; contingency: shorter notice for emergency maintenance with an agreed escalation process.

Can we set a 30-minute sync early next week (Mon/Tue) to run through the counters? If you prefer to exchange language first we can send a tracked-change order form.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Nimbus redlines to Order Form and SLA - initial

Irene / team — quick ops notes that should feed the counter:

- Uptime calculation: Redwood measures availability as "successful inference-serving time" / "total calendar time" for the billed capacity pool. We should add language that excludes scheduled maintenance windows (when notified) and events outside Redwood control (force majeure, third-party infra failures).
- Maintenance window notice: 72 hours is workable for standard maintenance. For security/emergency patches we need to reserve the right to do faster rollouts with post-facto notification and an expedited review process.
- Response times: proposed operational model:
  - P1 (system down): 1-hour ack, 4-hour mitigation target (24x7).
  - P2 (partial degradation): 2-hour ack, 1 business-day mitigation target (mon-fri business hours).
  - P3 (general request): standard business SLA (3 business days).
- Credit mechanics: credits applied as percentage of monthly service fees for the affected service pool. Recommend a cap of 30% of monthly invoice per incident and 100% annual cap across incidents.

I'll add these to the SLA matrix and flag language that is likely to trigger legal pushback (liability cap, exclusion clauses).

—Dev
Dev Patel
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Nimbus redlines to Order Form and SLA - initial

Laura / team — operational comments from CS / onboarding perspective: 

- Escalation path: we'll provide a named contact list for both Redwood on-call and account CSMs. For Nimbus production incidents we'll require a primary CSM + SRE on the 24x7 roster.
- Response windows: Dev's matrix looks reasonable. One addition: during the initial 90-day ramp we can offer accelerated response (P1 mitigation target of 2 hours) as part of the onboarding package.
- Maintenance notifications: 72 hours notice works for scheduled upgrades. For maintenance that is limited to non-critical subsystems we can allow 48 hours. We need to clearly define what constitutes "degraded performance" vs "service interruption".
- Credits & SLAs: CS prefers a tiered credit that is capped monthly (suggest 25% monthly cap) and an annual cap to protect operations. We'll mark the areas in the attached matrix where we need legal wording tweaked.

If Nimbus wants to accept the operational counters we can issue a tracked-change Order Form and push this to legal for final language.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Nimbus redlines to Order Form and SLA - initial

Irene / team — thanks for the quick turn. Nimbus accepts many of the operational clarifications; a few open items: 

- Uptime target: Nimbus still prefers 99.95% as our baseline for production-critical services. If Redwood cannot commit to that as a standard, can Redwood offer a premium "Committed Availability" add-on (priced higher) that includes 99.95 and a reduced credit cap?
- Emergency maintenance: Nimbus will accept a shorter-notice exception for security fixes if Redwood documents the emergency criteria and notification procedure.
- Credits cap: Nimbus is open to a monthly cap but wants the annual cap to be >50% of annualized fees only in the event of repeated major outages (we'll propose language).

I attached the signed NDA as requested (NDA_Signed.pdf). If Redwood can send a tracked-change Order Form reflecting the counters in the SLA matrix and an option for a "Committed Availability" add-on, we can aim to finalize signatures this week.

Best,
Laura
